tone_statements.quote: Kifuliiru, a Bantu J (Interlacustrine) language of the Shi‑Havu cluster, spoken in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, presents an interesting tone study in that it has undergone tone reversal with regard to proto‑Bantu. The tonal system of Kifuliiru is described at length in Van Otterloo (2011), chapter 3. Verb roots in Kifuliiru fall into three classes: High (H), Low (L) and toneless (Ø). The lexical tone (if any) of the verb always appears in stem‑initial position. [...] Every Tense/ Aspect/ Mood (TAM) includes one of six melodies: H, L, HL, LH, HH or LL.

sources.note: No statement on stress/accent. Says contour tones occur exclusively in the penult, every penult receives a second tone node before tone assignment (p.387); phrase-final H realized as short fall (L% boundary); long vowels shorten when followed by 3+ morae in the word. Tone (H/L/toneless roots, melodic TAM tones) only.

tone.says: First-hand tonology of the verb: Kifuliiru has undergone tone reversal relative to Proto-Bantu; verb roots are lexically H, L or toneless; extensions toneless except passive/causative (floating H); every TAM carries one of six melodic patterns (H, L, HL, LH, HH, LL); melodic tone docks on the leftmost free TBU, remaining tones link from the right edge; contour tones only in the penult (every penult gets a second tone node); final vowel usually extratonal; rules incl. Meeussen's Rule, LH raising…
